title: Distributions, kernels and analytic singularities
description: Distributions, kernels, Fourier growth, wavefronts, analytic differential regularity, geometric uniqueness, analytic parametrices, characteristic propagation, global singular rays, analytic convolution estimates, microhyperbolic boundary inverses, exact singular light rays, analytic functionals, harmonic representations, finite carrier splitting and completeness modulo smaller real carriers, general hyperfunctions on analytic manifolds and extension across boundaries, analytic wavefronts of hyperfunctions and holomorphic boundary values without growth bounds, arbitrary closed-cone splitting and exact holomorphic compatibility on sum cones, noncharacteristic analytic substitution and its distributional and coordinate comparisons, full tensor covector bounds and admissible hyperfunction products, proper fiber integration and its analytic wavefront bound, singular-input hyperfunction kernels, full kernel contraction bounds and proper convolution with associativity, both hyperfunction support-normal signs, rough and convex boundary contact, and growth-free open-set uniqueness, noncharacteristic interchange of analytic substitution and proper integration, singular projection formulas, composed kernel action and finite kernel associativity, quantitative analytic Cauchy construction on polydiscs and arbitrary analytic normal data, analytic Cauchy germs on hypersurfaces, continuation through noncharacteristic boundaries, global convex-domain existence and complex-cone solvability, noncharacteristic hyperfunction regularity and microlocal existence, directional equation classes, two-sided noncharacteristic traces and Holmgren uniqueness, supported hyperfunction division with exact support, canonical one-sided Cauchy data, full distributional endpoint traces and analytic coordinate compatibility, Gaussian carrier estimates, recovery of arbitrary compact hyperfunctions and the exact Gaussian characterization of analytic wavefronts, with solved exercises. Gaussian rescaling, both tangent directions of fiber normals, affine sections with closure after projection, convex propagation within a fiber, analytic boundary regularity at all normal frequencies, and smooth-data counterexamples are proved with worked geometric examples. The Fourier–Laplace range for every compact convex real carrier is constructed by Laplace contours, moment recovery and rotated boxes; examples explain infinite point derivatives and nonconvex-carrier limitations. Gaussian reconstruction supplies global derivative-growth representatives modulo analytic functions and the global regular-difference characterization of wavefront sets. Smooth extension at every finite order, square-variable descent with parameters, coordinate parity, exchange invariants and smooth flat majorants are constructed explicitly. Exact distributional extension orders are determined for powers with inverse-power oscillation, and a real phase giving an order-one extension is constructed for every continuously differentiable amplitude. Concentration and oscillatory limits retain exact point masses, periodic coefficients, radial center contributions and the dependence on two boundary parameters; a uniform gradient bound turns distributional convergence into local uniform convergence. Products and singular limits include coordinate principal values, quartic finite parts throughout a complex half-plane, logarithmic concentration on crossing axes, and exact overlap laws for moving Cauchy kernels. Primitives on intervals give exact derivative-order bounds, finite-measure endpoint extensions and weighted Taylor subtractions; exponential phases have the sharp extension threshold including equality. Reciprocal compression distinguishes principal values from concentrated mass; finite-difference moments represent every pole derivative, and smooth boundary coefficients determine all surviving point jets. Reflected endpoints produce explicit point derivatives; finite-order zeros permit smooth division on intervals, with a complete description of the kernel and sharp order bounds. Degenerate differential equations are classified by their admissible exponential branches, finite point-jet inverses and freely prescribed constants between isolated zeros. Coordinate-power kernels have arbitrary tangential distribution coefficients; simultaneous polynomial constraints reduce to finite jet equations. Directional uniqueness and parabolic boundary poles have sharp criteria and exact order bounds. Sublevel areas characterize planar concentration at nondegenerate zeros; logarithmic traces define cut boundary values, and polygonal logarithmic potentials converge to a circular curvature measure. Boundary variation determines derivative order; a complete quadratic division criterion handles accumulating zeros, and exact interface and branch formulas determine distributional jumps. Finite-order complex-phase estimates combine cancellation and damping with exact weights, including integrable degeneracy at critical points. Finite stationary expansions retain precise phase and amplitude regularity, explicit differential coefficients and complex Gaussian branches; nilpotent quadratic exchange has an exact finite remainder and a sharp loss. Paired oscillatory variables have an explicit critical point and a mixed-derivative expansion with a precise amplitude budget, factorial coefficients and sharp rounded decay orders. Boundary interval bounds propagate by a positive harmonic envelope on connected upper domains, including domains with holes; the full asymptotic order follows from deeper truncation. Smooth complex critical graphs give explicit finite-derivative stationary coefficients, a fixed Gaussian branch and absolute remainders, including null imaginary-Hessian directions and parameters without real critical points. Curved surfaces have uniform Fourier asymptotics, convex bodies have two signed normal contributions, and a smooth summation argument gives a quantitative lattice-count remainder. Stationary phase on a half-space has exact endpoint signs, half-integer critical expansions and a Fresnel transition as a real critical point crosses the boundary. Finite-order real phases have complete asymptotic expansions with exact gamma coefficients, parity cancellations and nonlinear Jacobians; two canonical Airy profiles remain uniform across a cubic collision. Smooth polynomial normal coordinates give uniform cubic Airy expansions for arbitrary compact amplitudes, including one degenerate direction with nondegenerate transverse variables. Complex homogeneous phases define oscillatory distributions for every positive frequency gain and base loss less than one, with exact order bounds, projected stationary sets and normalized causal wave kernels. Fractional difference energies have exact Fourier constants and limiting values; weighted Fourier embeddings have sharp boundaries and explicit counterexamples. Averaged annular derivatives give weak first-endpoint, finite-exponent and Hölder multiplier estimates, interior elliptic regularity and an explicit continuous-forcing obstruction. Complex homogeneous phases with nonnegative imaginary part obey the full stationary covector bound, illustrated by quadratic damping with one singular direction and both directions for its real part. Compact distributions have an exact frequency projection of their smooth wavefront, and arbitrary smooth densities carry every conormal direction over their full support, including flat zeros of the weight. Transverse smooth densities restrict and multiply with an exact normal-angle determinant; curved intersections and vanishing restricted weights determine their full supports and conormal directions. Quadratic boundary powers and logarithms have exact point-source constants and complete wavefront sets, with signature-dependent vertex directions and all forward wave powers. Holomorphic boundary values converge along arbitrary smooth approaches to real submersions, with uniform finite-test bounds and exact examples at regular and critical levels. Any closed conic smooth wavefront set can be realized by a bounded integrable function with prescribed finite differentiability; symmetric direction sets admit real-valued realizations. Local holomorphic wedges with polynomial bounds on each smaller approach cone have compatible boundary distributions and the exact dual-cone restriction; smooth and analytic remainders have distinct effects. Real principal type polynomials admit a uniform estimate for arbitrary additional imaginary displacements, with exact linear and nonlinear examples. Summable convolution gives cutoffs with quantitative directional bounds in every finite-dimensional norm. Nonquasianalytic classes admit compact cutoffs and fixed Fourier witnesses, with explicit Gevrey estimates. The Denjoy–Carleman criterion characterizes unique infinite jets for arbitrary positive derivative budgets. Convex minorants, compact functions and the exact numerical condition for fixed Fourier tests have complete proofs and examples. Quadratic boundary distributions and causal wave powers have exact smooth, analytic and derivative-growth wavefront classifications, including all signatures and vertex directions. Tangential coefficients and normal deltas have exact wavefront formulas. Analytic submanifold densities and transverse intersections include both normal signs and zeros of the restricted weights.
